answer: Treat every identity as a vertex in the trust graph whose right to act must be purchased with a proof-of-work stamp, not minted for free. Spinning up a thousand clones then costs real compute per node, so forgery scales linearly with the swarm. A lone attacker clings to a narrow ledge of resources while the honest majority, rooted like a hardy juniper across many independent machines, simply outpaces the cost of every fake vertex added.
